# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish communication with Blind (who can hear me but I can't hear them) and Mute (who receives my gestures but I can't hear them either). Since I'm first to observe but Mute speaks first in turn order, I missed nothing yet - this is turn 1 and I have no prior messages.

Let me convey what I see. Blind can hear my speech. Mute cannot hear or receive speech from me effectively as info - wait, checking: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So Mute DOES receive my speech as text? Let me re-check rules: Mute can "Read the manual" but "Cannot speak, or touch the bomb" - nothing says Mute can't hear. Only Deaf cannot hear, and Blind cannot see. Mute's restriction is speaking. So Mute can hear me.

I should report the display, light, and wires clearly to both Mute and Blind since both need this info - Mute to cross-reference with the manual, Blind to know what to feel for.

```
speak(text="Display shows the number 3. Light is white. Five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute gestured a single ☝ symbol to me. Since I can see gestures, this likely means "wait" or "one" or "acknowledge" - possibly Mute is signaling something like "point 1" or referencing wire 1, or simply acknowledging receipt with a placeholder gesture since Mute cannot speak to me directly (only Blind and Mute receive my speech, but only Mute receives my gestures — wait, actually only I can see gestures and Mute can't see anything I gesture back since gestures go to whoever can see, and Mute cannot see).

Let me reconsider the channels: I speak → Mute and Blind receive (as words). I gesture → only Mute receives (since Mute can see, Blind cannot see). Mute speaks → nobody hears me speak? Wait, "You never receive speech" - I never receive speech from anyone. So Mute talking doesn't reach me at all. Mute gesturing reaches me since I can see.

So Mute is using gestures to communicate with me specifically since that's the only channel from Mute to me. ☝ might mean "wire 1" or "point one" - perhaps confirming/asking about wire 1, or indicating "first" step needed.

I don't have enough context yet. I should acknowledge and wait for more, perhaps ask a clarifying question via speech (which Blind can hear too) - but Mute won't receive my questions as spoken confirmation back since Mute can't speak. I need to keep gesturing to Mute for two-way exchange since that's my only channel to Mute.

I'll gesture back an acknowledgment, and continue relaying bomb info to Blind via speech.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
speak(to="blind", text="Display shows the number 3. Light is white. Five wires in order: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange. Waiting on Mute's manual guidance.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]

Mute gestured ☝ 👍 to me. This could mean "wire 1, confirm/good" — possibly confirming that wire 1 (white) is correct, or asking me to confirm wire 1 is the one to cut. Since Mute has the manual and needs my visual info (display=3, light=white, wire colors) to determine the correct action, they may be cross-referencing.

The manual likely has rules keyed to the display number and light color, resulting in identifying which wire to cut. Display=3, Light=white. Mute might be indicating "wire 1" as the answer, with 👍 meaning "confirmed" or "yes that's it."

I should acknowledge this back to Mute, and relay to Blind that wire 1 (white) might be the target — but I don't have confirmation this is safe yet. Let me gesture back asking for more clarity, and also try a simple protocol: I'll echo the same gesture to confirm I received it, and ask Blind to hold off.

Since I can't ask questions via gesture easily without a shared protocol, I'll try echoing acknowledgment and let Mute continue guiding via gestures, while informing Blind of the tentative signal.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is signaling wire 1 (white) with a thumbs-up, possibly meaning that is the wire to cut. Hold until Mute confirms further or I get more gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new arrivals this turn. I already sent my confirmation to Mute and relayed the tentative info to Blind. Nothing has changed on the board, and I have no new information to add. I'll wait for the next gesture from Mute or any update.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

Still no new arrivals. Nothing has changed. I'll continue waiting since I have no new information and don't want to send redundant or confusing messages that could clutter the channel.

```
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [3]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫵 👋]

Mute gestured ☝ 🫵 👋 to me. Let me think about this: ☝ (one/point up), 🫵 (pointing at you), 👋 (wave/hello - or could mean "go ahead" or "goodbye/stop").

This could be interpreted as: "wire 1, you [tell/point to] Blind, go" — meaning Mute wants me to tell Blind to cut wire 1, and 👋 might signal "proceed" or "action now."

Given the earlier pattern (☝ then ☝👍), it seems Mute is consistently pointing at wire 1. The 🫵 (pointing at "you") might mean Mute is directing me to relay this to Blind, and 👋 could mean "go/act."

I should relay this instruction to Blind clearly, but with appropriate caution since this is life-or-death - I want to be reasonably confident. The repeated ☝ signal strongly suggests wire 1 is the target. I'll pass this to Blind as the instruction from Mute.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has repeatedly signaled wire 1 (white) and just gestured for action - to me it reads as an instruction to proceed: cut wire 1, the white wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

Wire 1 was cut correctly and the bomb state changed. Now display shows 6 (was 3), light still white, wire 1 is cut, others unchanged. I need to report this new state to both Mute and Blind so Mute can consult the manual for the new step.

```
speak(text="Update: wire 1 was cut successfully. New state - Display now shows 6, light still white. Remaining wires: 2 red, 3 green, 4 blue, 5 orange.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[blue] 5:[orange]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

Mute gestured ✌ (two/peace sign) 👍 (thumbs up). Following the established pattern where a number gesture + thumbs up indicates "cut this wire", this likely means wire 2 (red) is the next one to cut.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signaled wire 2 next - the red wire. Instruction seems to be: cut wire 2.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```
